newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EU urges Estonia to speed adoption of EU laws.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Estonia to speed adoption of EU laws.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Hans van den Broek on Tuesday urged the Baltic state of Estonia to speed harmonisation of laws in line with EU legislation and continue working to integrate its large Russian population.

"I am impressed with the commitment to reform I meet everywhere and find the work to prepare for EU membership encouraging," van den Broek said in a statement during a two-day visit to the small nation of 1.5 million people.
"Nevertheless, much remains to be done in the field of single market legislation as well as in terms of law implementation and enforcement," he added.
Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic nations, has carved out an impressive reputation as a committed reformer, trying to throw off the legacy of 50 years of Soviet rule.
Like neighbours Lithuania and Latvia, it has set its sights on EU and NATO membership.
Van den Broek also discussed the situation of the 500,000 strong Russian minority in Estonia.

"We have also offered assistance in stepping up language training efforts which in our view would help accelerate certain naturalisation procedures in meeting the requirements for citzenship," he told a news conference. 151548 GMT apr 97
